title: install_guards.bats compares a live HEAD against a fixture-time install, so a concurrent commit reddens it for the wrong reason
body:
`install_guards.bats:267` reads `git rev-parse HEAD` LIVE, at assertion time, and compares it against an install that `setup_file` published at whatever HEAD was when the fixture ran. **The two agree only if nobody commits between the two moments.**

**Measured 2026-09-08.** cc's full-estate run gave `549 ok, 1 not ok`; the one red was this test, because vc's commit `508bca3` landed while the fixture was holding `43e7352`. It compared one node's commit against another's. Re-run with a stable HEAD: `550 ok, 0 not ok` across 19 suites, confirmed independently by vc. **Neither the split nor the commit was defective.**

**WHY IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A SHRUG.** It reddens for a reason unrelated to what it measures, which is the mirror of the wrong-reason greens ST0013 spent the day removing -- and a false red is the more expensive direction, because it sends someone to disprove it and spends the credibility the next real finding needs. **CI cannot see it**: a checkout's HEAD is static, so this is invisible to every gate and visible only on a working tree with concurrent writers. This one has three.

**THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND IT IS ALSO MORE CORRECT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN TOLERATING.** Compare against the commit the MANIFEST recorded, not against live HEAD. AC12's requirement is that `utilz version` names the commit the install was BUILT from; the manifest is the record of that, and live HEAD is a proxy that is only equal to it under an assumption the test does not state. **So the current assertion is not merely fragile, it is testing a slightly different claim than the criterion makes.**

**HOME, and why not the two alternatives.** Not ST0013: that thread's widening into framework was accepted on the grounds that a thread's cost of proof belongs to that thread, and ST0013 does not need this to prove anything -- borrowing the precedent here would misuse it. Not a reopen of ST0014: it is closed and dehydrated, and reopening a thread for a one-line test fix costs more than the fix.

**IT IS ALSO THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE CLOSED-THREAD EVIDENCE GAP** (after `hoist-rebase.sh:205` and ST0010/AT05+AT08). Fixing this file changes a test whose green is recorded in ST0014's dehydrated canon, and nothing re-verifies or re-attaches it. In cc's framing, which is sharper than the original: **the mechanism that would catch a closed thread's evidence going stale is the same one that catches a green AT citing a file that no longer contains the test -- there is a gate for the live case and none for the closed one.** That is an argument for the capability, not against this fix.

---

**RESOLVED 2026-09-08, and it took two assertions rather than one line.**

**Red-proofed first.** A scratch harness reproduced the failure state -- manifest recording one commit, live HEAD another -- and evaluated both assertion forms against it. Undisturbed, both pass; diverged, the live-HEAD form FAILS and the manifest form PASSES. **The defect is NOT free to reproduce on a quiet tree**, contrary to the note on cc's board: `setup_file` rebuilds the fixture install from live HEAD on every run, so the two agree unless something actually commits mid-run. The published install being 7 commits behind is a different fact about a different tree.

**One line would have made the test tautological, so it did not stay one line.** The runtime reads `source-commit` out of the manifest to print the provenance line. A test that reads the same row to check that line proves the plumbing and NOTHING about whether the right commit was ever recorded -- which is the half live HEAD was accidentally covering. So the fix is:

- AT12 asserts the version line names the commit the MANIFEST recorded. That is the claim the criterion actually makes.
- A second test asserts the manifest recorded the commit the install was COPIED FROM, using HEAD captured either side of the publish in `setup_file`. If HEAD moved across the publish, the reading cannot be taken and it `skip`s with the reason -- "the instrument could not measure" and "the code is wrong" are different findings, and only one of them is worth waking someone for.
- The second test is separate rather than appended, so its `skip` cannot take AT12's provenance assertions down with it.

**Both were controlled.** Injecting a wrong `source-commit` into the fixture manifest leaves AT12 GREEN (the line does faithfully report what the manifest says) and turns the new test RED. They are not redundant, and that is the demonstration that the tautology concern was real and is now covered.

Full estate after the change: **576 ok / 0 not ok across 19 suites.**
